If it doesn't work out for me, what are my options?
• Just now
Seen • Just now
If it doesn’t work out, you’ve got a few practical options depending on what you mean by “doesn’t work out.”
If you’re still in a trial and just need more time to decide, trial extensions aren’t self-serve, but you can ask for one in this chat and share what you still need to test.
If you want to stop your own Kajabi subscription, you can pause it (this is called a Parked Plan). From your Kajabi dashboard: 1) Click Settings (bottom left). 2) Click Billing. 3) Choose the option to pause your subscription (Parked Plan). This keeps your account active while you’re not paying.
If you’re trying to stop billing for a customer’s subscription or payment plan, you can pause payments: 1) Click Contacts. 2) Click the customer’s name → Open full profile. 3) Click Purchases. 4) Click More Info for the Offer. 5) Click the Offer → More Actions (…) → Pause Payments → confirm.
One important note: if a customer subscription is canceled, it can’t be reinstated; they’d need to re-purchase to resume billing.

To get the best result, use Kajabi in this order: validate your idea, build a simple sales page, then test the full purchase flow before you promote.
Start with the Foundations guide (9 steps): validate your idea, set brand colors, add instructor details, build a waitlist, connect a payment method, create your first product, price it, design your website, then test the whole purchase journey yourself.
Build your sales page around one offer (not multiple). 
Add clear headings, the “why” and “what,” social proof, a short “about you,” and a clear offer outline. 
Keep the path simple: avoid sending people away to a free download, newsletter, or blog post.
Test on desktop and mobile, click every button, and use a 100% off coupon to test checkout and confirmations.

Is there a subscription or refill option?
• Just now
Seen • Just now
Yes. Kajabi supports both a subscription option (recurring billing) and a payment plan option (split into installments). 
If you want a subscription (weekly, monthly, or yearly):
From your Kajabi dashboard, click Sales. 
Click Pricing.
Select the Offer you want to edit (or create a new one).
Click the Pricing tab.
In Payment Type, choose Subscription.
Set the billing interval (weekly, monthly, yearly), and (optional) add a trial period or setup fee.
Click Save.
If you want a refill-style option, that’s the same idea: set the subscription to bill monthly (or weekly) so customers keep paying to keep access.
